Ethical issues of AI

AI already decides bank loans, assists medical diagnoses and shapes our academic software. Is it fair? Is it transparent? Who is responsible when it fails?

BiasPrivacyDeepfakesBlack boxWorkforce
Daniela & Vicente
Pillar 01 / Bias & discrimination

Algorithmic bias

Machines are not neutral. They are trained on historical human data, and that data carries our prejudices.

  • HiringRecruitment tools penalized female applicants because past hiring favored men.
  • PolicingPredictive algorithms gave higher risk scores to minority communities.
Biased data → biased algorithms
Pillar 02 / Consent decay

Data privacy

Generative AI needs massive datasets, and much of that data was never given with permission.

  • ScrapingPersonal photos, code and behavioral logs taken from the web.
  • SurveillanceFacial recognition in public spaces threatens civil liberties.
  • GDPRRules exist, but convenience vs. privacy is still unresolved.
Pillar 03 / Synthetic media

Deepfakes

Generative tools can fabricate hyper-realistic video and audio of people who never said a word.

  • ScamsVoice cloning used for financial fraud.
  • ElectionsPolitical disinformation before democratic votes.
  • EducationUncritical AI use puts academic integrity at risk.
Verify → before you trust
Pillar 04 / Accountability

The black box

Neural networks decide through layers of statistics. Even the engineers who build them cannot fully explain the outcome.

If AI fails, who is responsible?
DeveloperInstitutionUser
XAI = Explainable AI
